summary: Drove the Oregon coast (Hwy 101) from Humbug Mountain State Park to Seattle, stopping at a near-empty beach, Sea Lion Caves, Thor's Well, Cape Kiwanda and Tillamook. A bike-rack hit on a parked car and a 1.5-hour advisor call delay pushed them into Seattle after midnight.
slept_at: Charles' family house, Seattle WA (arrived after midnight)
contacts: Taqueria Mendez, Tillamook OR (cook made steak burritos after the truck closed)
Charles' family, Seattle WA (late-night food and a place to sleep)
planning_notes: Sea Lion Caves (Oregon coast, Hwy 101): about $18 entry and a 200 ft descent; only about 30 sea lions in late August.
Thor's Well (Oregon coast): best near high tide, but a wave nearly took two riders off the rocks. Stay on high ground.
Little or no cell service on Hwy 101 between towns. A phone advisor call took over 30 minutes of troubleshooting. Make calls from towns.
Cape Kiwanda food was expensive; Tillamook is the cheaper food stop.
Tillamook Creamery was about to close when they arrived in the afternoon. Arrive earlier.
Van with bike rack backed out of a Tillamook parking spot and pierced another car's tail lights. Note left, owner filed an insurance claim. Check rack clearance and back out slowly.
Coast day of about 485 mi with stops ran past 3 pm. Plan fewer stops on long coastal driving days.

summary: Left Seattle and drove through North Cascades National Park (Gorge Creek Falls, a cold Diablo Lake swim, rowan berries), with a van gas-door problem and a failed propane stove along the way. They camped by Curlew Lake State Park in Washington.
slept_at: Curlew Lake State Park campground, WA (campsite right on the lake)
contacts: Charles' family, Seattle WA (breakfast and crisp peaches)
planning_notes: Propane camp stove would not work at Curlew Lake State Park; they made sandwiches instead. Stove problems continued for several more days.
Van gas-tank door would not close after a fill-up; they taped it shut. It fixed itself a couple of days later.
North Cascades National Park: the drive through the park with many overlooks ran behind schedule. Budget extra daylight.
Sheri's Sweet Shop in Winthrop WA: smoothies and chocolates; long ice-cream lines.
Roadside self-serve farm egg cooler on the highway near Winthrop; they paid in cash.
Anderson's Grocery in Republic WA is a good grocery stop before the campsite.

summary: Woke up very cold at Curlew Lake, WA, then fought a van fuel-fill problem, a dirty windshield, and the stove failure. They drove up Going-to-the-Sun Road to Logan Pass, where a couple offered help, and reached Duck Lake, MT after dark.
slept_at: Duck Lake Campground, MT (primitive, no running water)
contacts: Unnamed couple at Logan Pass, Glacier NP MT (offered their propane can and a small burner)
Leaning Tree Campground, MT (showers and laundry near Duck Lake)
planning_notes: Northeast Washington mornings were very cold in late August. Their tent had no rainfly and they were cold; keep the rainfly on. The Apgar Visitor Center in Glacier sells beanies and thick socks.
Gas pump near Kettle Falls WA: fuel cut off after about 5 seconds at two different stations. The problem later cleared up on its own. Allow time for fueling and try another pump.
Colville WA self-serve car wash: a dirty windshield at sunrise was a glare hazard. Clean it before the mountain roads.
Lake Pend Oreille (Idaho): no real overlooks; the path to the water is a steep, loose-rock descent.
Going-to-the-Sun Road (Glacier NP): very narrow in places, with a rock wall on one side and cliff on the other. Drive it in daylight.
Logan Pass visitor center closes in the evening; the ranger recommended a Hidden Lake sunset hike from there.
Leaning Tree Campground (MT, near Duck Lake): showers and laundry; cell signal too weak for calls.
Duck Lake campground (MT) is primitive with no running water; they arrived after dark.

summary: Drove from Duck Lake, MT through Browning and Helena, losing over two hours in Helena to failed stove troubleshooting before buying a working propane canister. They then rushed through Yellowstone to Old Faithful and reached Lizard Creek Campground in Grand Teton National Park after dark.
slept_at: Lizard Creek Campground, Grand Teton NP, WY (arrived after dark)
contacts: Montana Dinosaur Center, MT (front-desk staff were friendly and knowledgeable)
planning_notes: Duck Lake campground has no running water. Browning MT (Blackfeet Reservation headquarters) is the nearest stop with a cafe and water; the cafe is inside a casino.
Montana Dinosaur Center (on the US-89 route in MT): worth a bathroom stop; touchable T. rex bone and an active dig.
Helena MT has the only big hardware stores for many miles. The next major city after Helena is in South Dakota. Buy supplies there.

Propane failure: the large refillable tank, adapter and a new stove did not fix the problem. A small camping propane canister from an outdoor store worked. Test the full cooking setup before the trip and carry a spare canister.
Yellowstone: they only had about 3 hours, passing many springs and geysers without stopping. Old Faithful visitor center is about 15 min from the eruption. Allow a full day for the park.
Lizard Creek Campground (Grand Teton NP, WY) was reached after dark. Plan an earlier arrival.

summary: The longest drive of the trip so far (560 mi): from Lizard Creek, WY through Dubois, the Wind River foothills, Thunder Basin, Wright and Mount Rushmore to a dirt road into Sage Creek Campground in the Badlands, SD after dark.
slept_at: Sage Creek Campground, Badlands NP, SD (dark sky site, many campers)
contacts: National Bighorn Sheep Center staff, Dubois WY (suggested the Fish Hatchery road into the Wind River Range)
planning_notes: National Bighorn Sheep Center in Dubois WY: $5 for exhibits; the staff tip led to good high-country wildlife views.
Fish Hatchery road into the Wind River Range (WY): unpaved, with good views and mountain goats at high elevation. Bighorn sheep are often seen there in summer.
Wright WY gas station advertised showers at $20 per person; they skipped it. Lizard Creek Campground has no shower.
Thunder Basin National Grasslands (WY): very empty and dry. Plan water and fuel.
Mount Rushmore parking was $35; the evening history talk in the auditorium was good.
Dirt road from the Black Hills into Sage Creek (Badlands NP): over an hour of unpaved road, and the drive was in darkness. Coyotes howled near camp. The campground is dark sky certified.

summary: Bison and prairie dogs at Sage Creek Campground in the morning, then a Badlands drive and a long I-90 stretch east. They ended the day at a host family's house in Madison Lake, MN after Google Maps routed them onto a closed, muddy road.
slept_at: Host family's house (GRA Katie's parents), Madison Lake, MN
contacts: Katie (dorm GRA) and her parents, Madison Lake MN (hosts; dinner and showers)
planning_notes: Sage Creek Campground (Badlands NP, SD): bison walked through the campground and got very close to tents. Keep distance; bison can attack if provoked. Prairie dog town in the loop.
I-90 across SD and MN: about 3 days of long, mostly uneventful driving with few planned stops. Plan stops.
Sioux Falls SD: river and falls are a scenic stop.
Heavy rain near Madison Lake MN made unpaved roads very muddy. Google Maps routed them onto a closed road; do not follow closed-road routing.
No showers from Duck Lake MT to Madison Lake MN (about 3 days). Plan shower stops on long stretches.

summary: Announcement inviting MIT students to apply for the Spokes 2026 summer team via a Google Form. The post also points to flyer images that are not readable in text.
planning_notes: Applications for the Spokes 2026 team opened on Sept 14, 2025 through a Google Form linked from the blog.
